subject: How to set default geom with custom stat?

messages.author: 641d929e96c82906
messages.subject: How to set default geom with custom stat?
parts:
I've written a stat for the cumulative distribution of x, whose
purpose is similar to the histogram geom. The code is patterned after
StatBin in the ggplot2 source code.

In the simplest case I'd like to do
> qplot(x,data=df,stat="cumdist")
and automatically use geom_step and y = (proportion of observations <=
x).

The stat is mostly working, but I would appreciate help on the
following:

For this plot:
qplot(x,..p..,data=df,stat="cumdist")
the default geom_point is used even though I included
default_geom <- function(.) GeomStep
in the definition of StatCumdist.
On the other hand, if I don't specify y, the
default_aes <- function(.) aes(x=..x..,y = ..p..)
works as intended, but the geom appears as vertical lines from each
(..x.., 0) to (..x.., ..p..). Manually specifying e.g. geom="step" or
geom=c("step","point") works fine. How should I specify the default
geom?

How can I specify default y axis limits to c(0,1)?

Can I have a compound default_geom, like c("step","point")? And could
I make that conditional on the number of points in x, using GeomStep
if there are lots of points?


Thank you in advance for any help!

Best regards,
Jon Olav



StatCumdist <- proto(Stat, {
objname <- "cumdist"
desc <- "Cumulative distribution"
desc_outputs <- list(
x = "sorted data values",
n = "number of points <= x",
p = "proportion of points <= x"
)
required_aes <- c("x")

default_geom <- function(.) GeomStep
default_aes <- function(.) aes(x=..x..,y = ..p..)

calculate <- function(., data, scales, ...) {
x <- sort(data$x)
n <- seq(along=x)
p <- n / length(x)
return(data.frame(x=x, n=n, p=p))
}

examples <- function(.) {
df <- data.frame(x=runif(10),a=(runif(10)>0.3))
qplot(x,..p..,data=df,stat="cumdist")
qplot(x,..p..,data=df,stat="cumdist",geom=c("step","point"))
# I would like to shorten this to
# qplot(x,data=df,stat="cumdist")
}

})

stat_cumdist <- StatCumdist$build_accessor()
StatCumdist$examples()

On Thu, Sep 3, 2009 at 7:38 AM, Jon Olav Vik<jon...@gmail.com> wrote:
>
> I've written a stat for the cumulative distribution of x, whose
> purpose is similar to the histogram geom. The code is patterned after
> StatBin in the ggplot2 source code.
>
> In the simplest case I'd like to do
>> qplot(x,data=df,stat="cumdist")
> and automatically use geom_step and y = (proportion of observations <=
> x).
>
> The stat is mostly working, but I would appreciate help on the
> following:
>
> For this plot:
>    qplot(x,..p..,data=df,stat="cumdist")
> the default geom_point is used even though I included
>  default_geom <- function(.) GeomStep

This is a limitation of qplot - it always uses the point geom, unless
you override it in the call. Getting the code write so it works
correctly with user specified geoms and/or stats is very tricky. I'd
recommend creating a geom alias.

> in the definition of StatCumdist.
> On the other hand, if I don't specify y, the
>  default_aes <- function(.) aes(x=..x..,y = ..p..)
> works as intended, but the geom appears as vertical lines from each
> (..x.., 0) to (..x.., ..p..). Manually specifying e.g. geom="step" or
> geom=c("step","point") works fine. How should I specify the default
> geom?
>
> How can I specify default y axis limits to c(0,1)?

There's not really anyway to do this, but you can cheat and in
geom_cumdist, return a list containing the geom and a specification
for the y axis.

> Can I have a compound default_geom, like c("step","point")? And could
> I make that conditional on the number of points in x, using GeomStep
> if there are lots of points?

Not at a high level. See GeomSmooth for an example of combining two
geoms. You could also use this approach to switch between geoms.
